memory_lessons.applicability: The current reduction task holds launch geometry and the multi-stage schedule fixed, so a different CTA-local implementation is a useful contrast.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior explicit warp-centric candidate was valid on all 10 cases and measured 30.066 μs across three samples versus the 46.787 μs baseline. This is one measured candidate, not independent confirmation or proof of the cause; the T1 catalog reports source diversity of 1.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this CUB BlockReduce implementation under the same controller protocol and compare complete-run timings.

proposal.hypothesis: Using CUB BlockReduce for each 128-thread CTA may reduce the cost of the modulo-based shared-memory tree while preserving the existing one-value-per-thread load, launch configuration, scratch-stage schedule and final copy. This contrasts with the previously measured explicit warp-centric implementation; the complete-run controller measurement will determine whether the local algorithm helps independently of launch topology.

retained: Replace reduce0's modulo-based shared-memory reduction tree with cub::BlockReduce<T, 128>::Sum.
Load one input per lane and contribute zero for out-of-range tail lanes.
Keep the 128-thread launch, dynamic shared-memory launch argument, multi-stage scratch schedule and final copy unchanged.
